A native of [[Baltimore]],{{cite web|title=Jamel Artis|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/3059276/jamel-artis|website=ESPN.com|access-date=August 21, 2017}} he played college basketball for [[University of Pittsburgh]]. ==College career== From [[Notre Dame Preparatory School (Fitchburg, Massachusetts)|Notre Dame Prep]] in Massachusetts,{{cite web|title=Jamel Artis, Pittsburgh Panthers, Small Forward|url=https://247sports.com/player/jamel-artis-727|website=247Sports.com|access-date=August 21, 2017}} on April 12, 2013, he signed to play for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh Panthers]].{{cite web|title=Jamel Artis – Basketball Recruiting – Player Profiles – ESPN|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/119169/jamel-artis|website=ESPN.com|access-date=August 21, 2017}} As a freshman, Artis played at [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] coming off the bench. Following the [[2014–15 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season]], Artis was named All-ACC third team.{{cite web|title=ACCMBB Coaches Name 2015 All-ACC Team|url=http://www.theacc.com/news/accmbb-coaches-name-2015-all-acc-team-03-09-2015|website=theacc.com|access-date=August 21, 2017|language=en|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150314191930/http://www.theacc.com/news/accmbb-coaches-name-2015-all-acc-team-03-09-2015|archive-date=March 14, 2015}} Artis received All-ACC honorable mention honors as a senior.{{cite web|title=ACCMBB Coaches Name 2015 All-ACC|url=http://www.theacc.com/news/accmbb-coaches-name-2015-all-acc-team-03-09-2015|website=theacc.com|access-date=August 21, 2017|language=en|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150314191930/http://www.theacc.com/news/accmbb-coaches-name-2015-all-acc-team-03-09-2015|archive-date=March 14, 2015}} ==Professional career== ===Orlando Magic (2017–2018)=== After going undrafted in the [[2017 NBA draft]],{{cite web|title=Undrafted Free Agent Tracker • r/nba|url=https://www.reddit.com/r/nba/comments/6j351n/undrafted_free_agent_tracker/|website=reddit.com|date=23 June 2017 |access-date=August 21, 2017|language=en}} Artis signed a partially guaranteed contract to join the [[New York Knicks]]' [[2017 NBA Summer League]] roster on June 24, 2017.{{cite web|title=Doyle Earns NBA Summer League Invite|url=https://dailyknicks.com/2017/06/24/knicks-rumors-new-york-jamel-artis-partially/|access-date=August 21, 2017|date=June 24, 2017|archive-date=October 26, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211026212739/https://dailyknicks.com/2017/06/24/knicks-rumors-new-york-jamel-artis-partially/|url-status=dead}} He averaged 8.8 points, 2.4 rebounds and 1.4 assists for 18 minutes per game through five games.{{cite web|title=Grading Jamel Artis' Summer League campaign|url=https://www.postingandtoasting.com/2017/7/29/16031156/grading-jamel-artis-summer-league-campaign|website=postingandtoasting.com|date=29 July 2017 |access-date=August 21, 2017}} On August 18, 2017, Artis signed with the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|title=Knicks Sign Three Free Agents|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-sign-three-free-agents-0|website=NBA.com|date=August 18, 2017|access-date=August 21, 2017}} He was released during preseason training camp on October 4.{{cite web|title=Knicks waive Jamel Artis|url=https://twitter.com/NY_KnicksPR/status/915613777504161795/photo/1|website=Twitter.com|access-date=October 4, 2017|date=October 4, 2017}} Twelve days later, Artis agreed to a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Orlando Magic]], meaning a split in his playing time between Orlando and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Lakeland Magic]].{{cite web|title=Magic Sign Jamel Artis to Two-Way Contract|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-jamel-artis-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2017|access-date=October 21, 2017}} Artis made his NBA debut with Orlando on December 13, playing for a single minute in a 106–95 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. ===Agua Caliente Clippers (2018–2019)=== On September 24, 2018, Artis signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]] for training camp.{{cite web|title=Kings Announce 2018 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-announce-2018-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 24, 2018|date=September 24, 2018}} On October 7, 2018, Artis was waived by the Kings.{{cite web|title=Kings Waive Jamel Artis|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/blog/kings-waive-jamel-artis|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 8, 2018|date=October 7, 2018}} ===Levallois Metropolitans (2019–2020)=== On July 3, 2019, [[Levallois Metropolitans]] announced that Artis joined them.{{cite web|title=L'américain Jamel Artis au Metropolitans 92 !|language=fr|url=https://levalloismetropolitans.com/fr/actualites/2019-07-03/l-americain-jamel-artis-au-metropolitans-92|date=July 3, 2019|website=levalloismetropolitans.com|access-date=July 3, 2019|archive-date=July 6, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190706095942/https://levalloismetropolitans.com/fr/actualites/2019-07-03/l-americain-jamel-artis-au-metropolitans-92|url-status=dead}} He averaged 13.3 points, 4.1 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game. ===BC Juventus (2020)=== On September 21, 2020, Artis signed with [[BC Juventus]] of the [[Lithuanian Basketball League]].{{cite web |title=Juventus tab Jamel Artis |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Lithuania/news/645426/Juventus-tab-Jamel-Artis |website=Eurobasket |access-date=October 2, 2020 |date=September 21, 2020}} ===Chorale Roanne (2020–2021)=== On December 25, 2020, he has signed with [[Chorale Roanne Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/chorale-roanne-lands-jamel-artis/|title=Chorale Roanne lands Jamel Artis|date=December 25, 2020|newspaper=Sportando|language=en|access-date=April 21, 2021|last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }} In 26 games, he averaged 11.1 points, 2.7 rebounds, and 2.1 assists per game. ===Kyoto Hannaryz (2021)=== On August 31, 2021, Artis signed with [[Kyoto Hannaryz]] of the [[B.League]].{{cite web |title=Jamel Artis agreed terms with Kyoto Hannaryz |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/France/news/702766/Jamel-Artis-agreed-terms-with-Kyoto-Hannaryz |website=Eurobasket |access-date=August 31, 2021 |date=August 31, 2021}} ===Ionikos Nikaias (2021)=== On September 29, 2021, Artis signed with [[Ionikos Nikaias B.C.|Ionikos Nikaias]] of the [[Greek Basket League]].{{cite news |title=Ionikos Nikaias ink Jamel Artis |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/ionikos-nikaias-ink-jamel-artis/ |website=Sportando |access-date=September 29, 2021 |date=September 29, 2021|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} On November 1, he was released from the Greek club. ===NorthPort Batang Pier (2022)=== On December 31, 2021, Artis joined the [[NorthPort Batang Pier]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA) for the [[2021 PBA Governors' Cup]] as a replacement for the injured [[Cameron Forte]].{{cite web|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/northport-taps-a-new-import-in-james-gurley-artis-a793-20211231|title=NorthPort taps a new import in Greek league mainstay|website=Spin.ph|date=December 31, 2021|accessdate=December 31, 2021}} ===Cape Town Tigers (2022)=== In April 2022, Artis was revealed to be on the roster of the [[Cape Town Tigers]] for the [[2022 BAL season|second season]] of the [[Basketball Africa League]] (BAL).{{cite web |title=Cape Town Tigers (South Africa) |url=https://bal.nba.com/teams/cape-town-tigers-south-africa?view=roster |website=The BAL |access-date=7 April 2022 |language=en}} === Trepça (2022–2023)=== On December 12, 2022, Artis signed with [[KB Trepça|Trepça]] of the [[Kosovo Basketball Superleague|Kosovo Superleague]].{{cite web |title= Trepça zyrtarizon Jamel Artisin |url=https://asistionline.com/2022/12/12/trepca-konfirmon-lajmin-e-asist-it-zyrtarizon-jamel-artisin/ |website=asistionline.com |date=December 12, 2022 |access-date=8 May 2023 |language=sq}} Artis won the [[Kosovo Cup (basketball)|Kosovo Cup]] with Trepça.{{Cite news|url=https://telegrafi.com/trepca-mposht-sigal-prishtinen-dhe-fiton-kupen-e-kosoves/|title=Trepça mposht Sigal Prishtinën dhe fiton
